routePolicy: Only standard method.get(tag0)/post(tag2) and exact full path-with-query bytes /actions(8) or /action-result(14) admitted. Query, other, absent, malformed or arbitrarily long route stays unknown. No URL normalization, percent-decoding, query replay or raw text output. Route classification is not assertion that every method/path pair is an intended application endpoint.

corrState.missing: Admitted method/path; fields.get of fixed syntactically valid literal returns0 values: corrCount0,corrnull.
corrState.valid: Admitted method/path; exactly1 field-value, exactly64 bytes, each ASCII0-9/a-f; copy64 to fixed snapshot then publish corrCount1 and that value.
corrState.invalid: Admitted method/path; exactly1 value with any other length/byte shape, including empty/comma-coalesced/uppercase/newline: corrCount1,corrnull.
corrState.duplicate: Admitted method/path; at least2 returned values, even identical: corrCount2 saturated,corrnull. No wire-duplicate inference.
corrState.unknown: Method or path unadmitted; regardless of observed headers clear correlation/count to null. Preserve separately known method/path enum; unknown is never interpreted as missing.

ownership: Borrow original incoming-request for metadata; acquire one owned fields child, fields.get returns copied list values, drop fields child immediately on successful getter return, classify/copy only returned slices, then forward original owned request/outparam once. No body resource, request reconstruction, header mutation or uncertain-transfer retry.

memory.allocator: Checked wasm32 realloc(old,oldLen,align,newLen) with power-of-two alignment, unsigned overflow/end checks, min(oldLen,newLen) copy for nonzero-old growth/shrink, zero-size release returning0. Bump/frees reset only at next legal synchronous invocation; no realloc host/WASI calls.

allocatorFailure: Returned method.other/path strings and nested header lists can request arbitrary allocation before classification. The fixed guest bound does not bound host allocation. OOM/invalid allocation can trap BEFORE forwarding, possibly while fields child is live; no successful-forward/fallback/harmlessness guarantee. Resource cleanup of a trapped instance is not inferred.

abi.methodOrder: get0,head1,post2,...,other9; distinct from former native callback POST1.
abi.methodAndPathResult: 12-byte/alignment4 variant or option; discriminantbyte+0,ptr+4,len+8. Sync lower args(request,retptr).
abi.headersResult: own fields directly returned as one i32 canonical handle.
abi.fieldsGetResult: args(fields,namePtr,nameLen,retptr), list pointer+0/count+4; nested byte-list entries stride8/alignment4 pointer+0/length+4.
abi.stdoutResult: result tag1024, stream-error tag1028, own error1032; trailing return pointer.
abi.canonicalOptions: memory+realloc+UTF8 for method/path/fields.get; memory for stdout.write; unchanged simple own-transfer lower/lift.

joinPolicy: Require complete finalized raw capture and exact typed schema; missing/malformed/limited output stays unobserved.
One unique valid POST/actions candidate must match the declared public value alongside browser/NetLog and other public-lane evidence; value is public metadata, never a private ID.
Any competing invalid/duplicate/unknown POST or unknown-method candidate, including route-cleared records, conservatively blocks the corresponding join.
Missing/count0 may be a separate uninstrumented candidate only when method/path were admitted. Unknown must never be defaulted to missing.
Known GET observations are distinct, including forwarding/navigation; equal public values do not make them POSTs or establish outer-to-inner causal identity.
Do not concatenate records by local count, order, time or equal value into physical instances/Stores.
init: Only constants/globals/memory declarations; no core start or imported calls at instantiation. No manifest/environment/clock/entropy/filesystem access.
positiveWitness: Metadata snapshot before transfer plus ordinary code after the exact synchronous imported handler returned, conditional on independently validated new envelope/post-return structure. Not observer own return/post-return, host/TCP/task completion, identity, cause or fullNext.
